podcast.title: The Cure's "Job Application" Band
podcast.body: Cult Hero was essentially The Cure performing under a pseudonym, specifically designed by Robert Smith as a way to test out new bassist Simon Gallup in 1979 without official commitment. Robert, Simon, Robert's two sisters, and other friends secretly recorded a single, "I'm a Cult Hero," with Robert's mailman, Frank Bell, on lead vocals to further conceal their identities. "That's essentially the cure trading as Cult Hero, with Robert Smith's postman on lead vocals."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lineup Audition with Cult Hero
xref.body: In 1979, Robert Smith faced lineup issues, particularly regarding a bass player for The Cure. To thoroughly assess Simon Gallup as a potential fit, Smith orchestrated a "complete and full mock-up" in secret, forming the pseudonymous band Cult Hero to record a single with Gallup. This allowed Smith to confirm his compatibility with Gallup before officially bringing him into The Cure, alongside guitarist Paul Thompson, who had been in an earlier version of the band. "Robert found that he liked working with Simon, and guitarist Paul Thompson, who had been in an earlier version of the cure, was brought in, and now we have a new line up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
